notes: Small sample: 1 model (claude-haiku-5-5), 10 tasks x 1 sample = 10 generations per language, 40 total (scope cut from the planned 240 by a hard deadline). All 40 scripts passed, so this is a ceiling effect: the run cannot rank the languages. Wilson 95% intervals at 10/10 are [0.72, 1.00] for every language, so true rates anywhere from about 72% to 100% are consistent with the data. Each generation ran via `claude -p` with --tools "", --strict-mcp-config, --setting-sources "", a one-line system prompt, --no-session-persistence and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1, from an empty cwd (a smoke test showed ~755 input tokens, no CLAUDE.md). Success = exact match of stripped stdout within a 10 s timeout. Tools are one Python mock host invoked per call by every binding, so fixtures, errors and state (retry counters, the concurrency cap, duplicate-fetch detection) are identical across languages. Fairness caveats: Lua has no native concurrency, so the concurrency task degrades to sequential calls there (the prompt allows this; the Python, JavaScript and bash scripts each reached exactly 3 calls in flight, Lua ran 1 at a time); bash gets jq and parses JSON on stdout plus error JSON on stderr, while the others get decoded values and exceptions; bash's no-other-interpreters rule is stated in the prompt, not enforced by PATH (no generated bash script used one). Luau was skipped (no luau CLI installed, and the cut scope excluded it).
